key_insight: A cμ priority rule using effective service rates that account for compute, memory bandwidth, and KV-cache capacity is optimal in a fluid model of LLM inference scheduling.
engineering_relevance: Memory-aware request prioritization can reduce serving latency while preserving high throughput under limited GPU KV-cache capacity.
method: Reduce stochastic prefill and decode scheduling to a multiclass single-server fluid queue.
Prove cμ optimality for cumulative holding cost and, for finite workloads, completion time and full-run output-token throughput.
Construct a feasible finite-system policy and prove its scaled dynamics converge to the optimal fluid policy.
evidence_signal: Experiments on a real LLM serving engine with an NVIDIA H800 report substantially lower average latency and sustained high throughput relative to existing scheduling policies; the abstract provides no numerical results.
watch_item: The optimality guarantees rely on fluid scaling, so finite-system performance and effective-rate estimation require validation under deployment-specific workloads.
paper_title: Asymptotic Optimality of $cμ$-Rule for LLM Inference Scheduling under Memory Constraint
